correctness.rationale: For each of eight anchors, the attached verifier independently constructs a length-2048 prefix in two ways, counts every distinct length-L factor in two encodings, checks that p(4)=12 or p(L)=4L as appropriate, and tests all block sizes m<=r for every factor. Each upper bound is verified over a factor set complete for the infinite word by Allouche's theorem. In each row there is a concrete factor failing every m<r, proving sharpness. The proved monotonicity R(k)<=R(k+1) fills all intermediate orders 6,7,10,...,15. The first-source identity and boundary conventions were explicitly checked, and no finite sample is mistaken for infinite completeness without the published theorem.

originality.rationale: The asserted all-start *sharp* radius for the regular paperfolding word is strictly stronger than known occurrence/existence and generic-growth results, which do not specify these exact threshold values. The closest exact radius result for the Fibonacci word addresses a different infinite word and cannot imply paperfolding values. The original factor-count theorem serves as a tool, not prior coverage of the anti-power classification. Relevant full texts were compared by quantified statements, and accessible scientific records were compared for overlap. Risk: a missed unindexed paperfolding table could cover the finite values.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named prior tables of paperfolding anti-power block lengths could have the same small-order values.
The exact Fibonacci-radius publication was comparable by published summary, not full repository text.
The result depends on the correctness of the independently published Allouche factor-complexity theorem; it has not been independently audited as part of this project.

value.rationale: The first sharp worst-position anti-power radius spectrum of the canonical paperfolding word refines general at-every-position existence, quantifies the natural first dyadic blocks through 16, and identifies a surprisingly abrupt first post-dyadic boundary at order 17 (9 to 15). This is a motivated exact finite cutoff tied to the intrinsic binary word and anti-power-order parameter, not an arbitrary isolated length-n count, and gives a concrete test case for the literature's broader quantitative anti-power questions.
